newsitem.title: UK: UK seen producing bumper 96 cereals output - Dalgety.
newsitem.headline: UK seen producing bumper 96 cereals output - Dalgety.

text.p: Britain's total cereals output from the current crop is expected to reach 24.57 million tonnes, the highest level since 1986/87 before the introduction of set-aside, a leading Britain grains trader said on Thursday.

Wheat production would reach 15.90 million tonnes, barley 7.98 million and oats 690,000 tonnes, said Andrew Barnard, UK arable crop marketing manager for Dalgety Agriculture, the agribusiness arm of Dalgety plc.
All figures were up on 1995 when wheat output totalled 14.30 million tonnes and oats 750,000 tonnes. This year's barley output was 1.0 million tonnes higher, he told a news conference.

Barnard said the record crop could be attributed to an estimated increase in the overall 1996 cereal area at 3.8 percent over 1995 and higher yields in both wheat and barley. But there were also differences in quality between autumn and spring crops, with the spring crops producing disappointing yields due to poor establishment followed by dry conditions.
"A late season, combined with intermittent rainfall, has lengthened the harvest period and has caused quite market geographic variation in quality and yield," Barnard said.

"There certainly have been geographic variations and some disappointing crops but the potential of plant breeding since the record 1984 crop has shown through as the result of the season's climatic conditions and continues the improvement trend," he said.
